description: Contract-level binary vulnerability detection comparison on the same 217-contract benchmark. N_valid = contracts successfully processed. Invalid contracts treated as negative for strict metrics.
evaluation_protocol: contract_positive = tool emits at least one mapped vulnerability finding for the contract.

baselines.note: Best Slither variant (any severity positive). Achieves 0 recall on DeFiHackLabs and Web3Bugs (no DeFi-focused detectors).

Applies the LLM directly to the target function's PDG facts and source, with no retrieval hypothesis and no SMT witness. The prompt is in results/baselines/direct_llm_prompt.py. FPR ties MechaAudit's full pipeline, but recall collapses without retrieval-supplied mechanism hypotheses and solver-backed guard-absence evidence.
2 project evaluations timed out, excluding 7 contracts (N=210, 69 vulnerable and 141 safe).
37 invalid cases treated as negative for strict metric. Precision improves vs Qwen variant but recall remains low.

No official retrieval assets for LogicScan were found anywhere online; those assets are the key material for LogicScan to achieve good performance. The results reported here are from a test without such assets (audit-only mode).

121 projects processed, 0 valid findings under local Qwen3-32B. The original Knowdit paper uses GPT/Claude in a specialized agent-and-fuzzing environment; that environment was not reproduced here. The results are not directly comparable.
